CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). (4) The AgentDriver-vs-OperatorGateway distinction recorded here is PRESERVED and now realised: the SDK adapter is the agent-facing side, and the OperatorGateway (event envelopes, hydration/reconnect, first-responder arbitration, WebSocket backpressure) is the operator-facing side. DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION: adversarial multi-model review of shipment 011-S (feature 012-F, checkSymlinkEscape's ECE3DAB7 dangling-intermediate fix) independently discovered and Ship empirically verified (live reproduction on this Windows host, confirmed reading an outside-root secret file through an accepted path) a DISTINCT, PRE-EXISTING CRITICAL containment bypass: a LIVE (non-dangling) Windows directory junction used as the FINAL path component of a Resolve() candidate is ACCEPTED even when its target is outside the workspace root, because os.Stat transparently follows IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT reparse points and filepath.EvalSymlinks never resolves them, so containment is never actually checked against the junction's real target. Requires no elevated privilege (junction creation, unlike symlinks, needs none). Verified via direct trace of Go 1.26.5 stdlib (os/stat_windows.go, os/types_windows.go, path/filepath/symlink_windows.go) AND via a standalone empirical reproduction test (not committed). ALSO confirmed PRE-EXISTING in main (git show main:internal/pathsafe/pathsafe.go): main's original checkSymlinkEscape used os.Stat unconditionally for every ancestor including the final component, so the identical bypass mechanism (Stat-follows-junction, EvalSymlinks-does-not-resolve-junction, hasPathPrefix-passes-lexically) exists byte-for-byte in main -- this shipment's dangling-symlink fix does NOT introduce or worsen it. Related: a LIVE junction used as an INTERMEDIATE ancestor is, as a side effect of 012.003-T's own Lstat-based ancestor-walk fix, now unconditionally REJECTED regardless of whether its target is inside or outside root (fails closed, not an escape, but a behavior change from main's more-permissive-but-also-buggy prior behavior; doc comment corrected in this shipment's own commit to accurately describe this as a known limitation rather than falsely claiming junctions are 're-resolved'). Out of scope for shipment 011-S per P-021 C1: 012-F's chartered scope (stash entries ECE3DAB7/CA469B3D/5FE4A7BE/5158769F/805248F7) is explicitly the DANGLING intermediate case only; this is a LIVE-junction defect never named in the feature's scope or anti-goals, discovered only during this shipment's own adversarial review. A durable fix requires detecting a live name-surrogate reparse point (junction/mount point) specifically and resolving its true target via a Windows-specific mechanism (e.g. GetFinalPathNameByHandle-equivalent semantics), or pinning GODEBUG=winsymlink=0 module-wide with regression coverage proving the verdict is stable across that setting (the current behavior is undocumented-toolchain-default-dependent -- Go 1.23+ winsymlink=1 causes this; winsymlink=0 would cause os/filepath to treat junctions as symlinks and likely close this, but that is an unverified, cross-cutting toolchain-behavior decision requiring its own deliberation, not a mechanical fix). Full independent verification, code trace, and empirical reproduction are recorded in docs/closure/2026-09-07-011-s-012-f-pathsafe-containment-adversarial-review.md (findings F0, F1, F3, F7).
